samples.summary: The delta's core change — the merge-expansion budget moves from `normalizeCellRange` (all callers) to `computeSelectionRects` only — has no test at the caller level
samples.evidence: `packages/docs/test/view/cell-range-expand.test.ts:196-277` only exercises `expandCellRangeForMerges` with the budget passed explicitly as an argument. Nothing asserts that `Selection.getNormalizedRange` (the delete/copy/cut path) now expands *exactly*, nor that `computeSelectionRects` still expands *bounded*. The two existing `getNormalizedRange` tests (lines 123-193) use 4x4/3x3 tables where the 1<<18 budget could never bind, so they pass identically before and after this change. Reverting `normalizeRange`'s default to `MAX_MERGE_EXPANSION_CELLS` — the exact regression the diff exists to prevent, whose symptom is a merged cell half-cleared by a cell-rectangle delete — would leave the whole docs suite green.

samples.evidence: The three new tests in `packages/docs/test/model/table-nesting.test.ts:180-260` call `capTableCellsNesting` directly with a hand-supplied `baseDepth`. verdict.reason: Verified the code: the budget is applied at exactly one call site, `computeSelectionRects` -> `normalizeRange(range, layout, MAX_MERGE_EXPANSION_CELLS)` (selection.ts:715), while `normalizeRange` (selection.ts:262-266), `normalizeCellRange` (selection.ts:202-206) and `expandCellRangeForMerges` (selection.ts:123-127) all default to `Infinity`, and `Selection.getNormalizedRange` (selection.ts:901-906) passes no budget. No test exercises that wiring. All three budget tests in cell-range-expand.test.ts:196-277 call `expandCellRangeForMerges` directly with the budget as an explicit argument (:236 `1000`, :257 default, :262 `4`, :275 `1 << 18`). The caller-level `getNormalizedRange` tests (cell-range-expand.test.ts:123-193; nested-table-cell-range.test.ts:348-409) use 2x2/3x3/4x4 tables where a 2^18 budget can never bind, and the only `computeSelectionRects` tests (selection-line-affinity.test.ts:82, image-selection-tint.test.ts:162) carry no `tableCellRange`. table-drag-merge-selection.test.ts drives real paint-path drags but over a 4x3 table. Wider sweeps (no test references MAX_MERGE_EXPANSION_CELLS, no mock/spy of selection.js, no large-table fixture outside cell-range-expand.test.ts, no cross-package test of docs selection.ts) produced no counterexample. Reverting normalizeRange's default to MAX_MERGE_EXPANSION_CELLS, or dropping the argument at selection.ts:715, would leave the docs suite green — a silently weakened guard whose symptom is a merged cell half-cleared on delete/cut. In-lane: changed behavior with no meaningful test.

verdict.reason: Verified independently. `pasteTableCells` (packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:4706) computes `cellBaseDepth = this.doc.tableNestingDepth(pos.blockId) + (cellInfo ? 0 : 1)` (:4719-4720) and feeds it to `capTableCellsNesting` at both write sites (:4730-4733, :4765-4768). No test reaches this code. Repo-wide greps for `pasteTableCells`, `capTableCellsNesting` and `cellBaseDepth` turn up only the src definitions, design/task markdown, two test *comments* (table-nesting.test.ts:193; table-merge-normalize.test.ts:41, which is explicitly a hand-written "mirror" of the write loop rather than a call), and three direct helper calls in packages/docs/test/model/table-nesting.test.ts:208/227/242 that each pass a hand-supplied baseDepth. I also followed the only indirect route: `pasteTableCells` is called solely from `applyPastePlan` (text-editor.ts:1575) for `plan.kind === 'tableCells'`, produced by `planPaste` (:1526, :1541) from an HTML/markdown table or an internal tableCells payload. Every test that dispatches a real paste event (copy-integrity.test.ts:483/813/901/1017, large-paste-indicator.test.ts:177-187) supplies a blocks/text payload with no `<table>` markup; a grep for `<table>|<td>|<tr>|<th>` across all *.test.ts matched only clipboard.test.ts's pure parser unit tests (620-815) and unrelated sheets tests. tableCells appears in tests only on the serialize/copy side (clipboard.test.ts:92-128, copy-integrity.test.ts:1368-1374, nested-table-cell-range.test.ts:257-259), never pasted back. There is no e2e directory and no frontend test referencing tableCells. So the branch-dependent `+1`, the `pos.blockId` anchor and the in-table branch's use of the caret depth are unpinned: an off-by-one either drops a legal nested table on paste or writes one past the cap, where the CRDT read path truncates it to a rowless table (table-nesting.test.ts:72-80 shows that shape), losing rows for every reader. Data-affecting and user-visible on a path users take, so major under the test-adequacy rubric.

verdict.reason: The truncated-rows refusals in setHeader (yorkie-doc-store.ts:1015-1017, path [0]) and setFooter (1060-1063, path [children.length - 1]) have no test anywhere. All .setHeader/.setFooter calls in packages/frontend tests are the three margin/cache-offset tests at yorkie-doc-store.test.ts:2017/2033/2047, which use no nested tables and assert no throw. The new cap suite (yorkie-doc-store.test.ts:3646-3843) exercises only setDocument, insertBlockAfter, updateBlock and updateTableCell; the /never read/ refusal tests at 3797-3826 never touch header/footer. MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH occurs in only one other test file (src/components/history/__tests__/snapshot-adapters.test.ts), which tests the snapshot reader cap, not the store writers, and no other file builds nested-table chains. Neither guard branch is ever executed, so a wrong hand-computed path (never firing → replicated deletion of a peer's rows on a header rewrite, or always firing → legitimate header edits refused) ships undetected. Major under the missing-test rule for a guard whose failure loses peer-written data.
